what: The heuristic discovers customers and the depot from goal fact names, resolves their loc/visited facts once, and reconstructs a routing matrix from grounded visit, visit-via-depot, and return-to-depot operators using their metric costs. At evaluation it identifies the current location and unvisited customers, computes a Prim MST plus endpoint connectors, a directed minimum-exit relaxation, and a nearest-neighbor completion ending at the depot. It returns a blend of the strongest routing lower bound and the greedy completion estimate. It does not depend on optional capacity, demand, or max-vehicle PNE names.
why: CVRP states encode a partial route through the current loc and monotonic visited facts, while grounded operator names reliably expose all routing transitions and their compiled costs. MST and directed degree relaxations cheaply capture global spatial structure; the greedy completion adds route-order sensitivity that helps distinguish promising successor customers. This is especially useful for the representative Euclidean and clustered instances, where local proximity and expensive inter-cluster transitions strongly determine good routes. Avoiding folded resource expressions preserves correctness and generalization when capacity and demand variables are absent.
